title: Amortize rate-limit credits across multi-currency invoices and late-arriving usage
creator: Anika Patel
description: Summary: Customers that hit rate limits receive automated credits. We currently emit credits as single-line refunds in the export that are not amortized across multiple invoices when usage is billed in different currencies or when the credit is created after invoice generation due to late-arriving usage. This causes invoice-level mismatches in NetSuite leading to manual adjustments and customer confusion. Goal: implement deterministic amortization of rate-limit credits across affected invoices, preserve auditability, and ensure idempotent, currency-aware exports to Stripe/NetSuite.
acceptance_criteria: All rate-limit credits generated after invoice finalization must be split across affected invoice periods and exported as amortized adjustment lines referencing the original credit ID
Exports to Stripe and NetSuite must use invoice-time FX rates for currency conversion; exported totals must match ledger totals within 1 unit of smallest currency (cent/penny)
Backfill migration for the last 12 months completes with a reconciliation report showing zero net drift after amortization
Automated tests covering multi-invoice allocation, late-usage credit creation, and edge-case rounding are added to billing-reconciler CI
Canary rollout (5% accounts) shows no increase in manual support escalations and stable export idempotency
updates: 2026-02-12 - Anika Patel: Created ticket after incident INC-2026-02-08 where 4 enterprise invoices in EMEA had mismatched credit lines due to late-arriving rate-limit credits and EUR/USD conversion differences. Root cause traced to single-line credit export logic that assumes same-billing-cycle allocation.

2026-02-18 - Marco Rivera: Initial design proposal posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BILL/Rate+Limit+Credit+Amortization (see Design v1). Proposal includes a persistent 'credit_amortization' ledger table keyed by credit_id and invoice_id and a deterministic allocation algorithm using invoice timestamps and per-invoice FX snapshots.

2026-02-22 - Sasha Kim (Finance): Recommend using invoice posted FX rate for conversion rather than event-time rate; affects rounding behavior. Prefer earliest-invoice rounding bias to keep subsequent invoices clean for customer statements.

2026-02-25 - Design review: Decided to store allocation metadata on exported line items (export_metadata.credit_allocation_ref) so NetSuite and Stripe lines can be traced back to original credit. Trade-off: larger export payload vs auditability. Approved.

2026-03-01 - Marco Rivera: Proof-of-concept implemented. GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/3211 (includes allocation algorithm and unit tests for USD/EUR/JPY). Local benchmark: allocation step adds ~12ms per credit on worst-case multi-invoice split; acceptable for batch export windows.

2026-03-03 - QA notes: Found edge-case where a tiny residual (< 1 smallest currency unit) remained after even distribution across 7 invoices. Added deterministic residual strategy: apply leftover cents to earliest invoice (consistent with Finance guidance). Updated tests accordingly.

2026-03-05 - Ops: Added feature flag billing.amortize_rate_limit_credits to gate rollout. Migration plan drafted to backfill previous credits into amortization ledger for 12 months. Backfill will run as background job with progress logs to /dashboards/billing/backfill.

2026-03-08 - Marco Rivera: Integration PR opened to add allocation exports for Stripe and NetSuite: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/3248. Includes export schema bump and idempotency keys referencing original credit_id and allocation sequence.

2026-03-09 - Finance: Reviewed export schema; requested a reconciliation report that shows original_credit_id, allocated_invoice_id, amount_in_currency, fx_rate_used, and rounding_residual. Report CSV format agreed.

2026-03-10 - Marco Rivera: Started canary deployment to 5% of accounts with feature flag on. Monitoring knobs: support-escalations Slack alert, billing-export-error-rate, net_reconciliation_drift metrics. Initial 24h check shows 0.02% change in export error rate (within noise).
implementation_notes: Create credit_amortization ledger table: columns credit_id, invoice_id, allocated_amount_minor_units, currency, fx_rate_snapshot, allocation_seq, created_at

Allocation algorithm: build list of impacted invoices sorted by invoice.posted_at; compute allocation by normalizing credit to invoice currency using invoice_fx_rate, distribute floor(amount / n) to each, and apply residual to earliest invoices
Export changes: include export_metadata.credit_allocation_ref=(credit_id:allocation_seq) and idempotency_key including original credit_id and allocation_seq
Backfill: iterate credits generated in 12-month window, compute allocation using historical invoice FX snapshots, write amortization records and emit reconciliation CSV for Finance review
Monitoring: add billing.metric credit_amortization_unallocated_count, credit_amortization_export_failures, reconciliation_drift_cents
Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> 25% -> 100% with backfill running after 25% step
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: FX snapshots for very old invoices may be missing. Mitigation: fallback to daily market FX snapshot with audit flag and include fallback reason in reconciliation CSV.

Risk: Increased export payload may hit NetSuite mapping limits. Mitigation: coordinate with Finance to validate NetSuite import templates; if needed compress allocation refs into single reference object and store details in internal reconciliation CSV.

Risk: Rounding could cause small customer-visible drifts. Mitigation: deterministic residual strategy and finance-approved rounding policy; surface small adjustments to accounts team for manual review if above threshold
Risk: Backfill large volume may increase DB load. Mitigation: throttle backfill with rate limit and run from read-replica where possible
next_steps: Complete integration PR review and merge (GH #3248)
Run 72h canary with monitoring thresholds, then expand to 25% if stable
Start backfill for 12 months in paused mode; validate first 1000 credits and hand off CSV to Finance
Add final e2e tests for Stripe+NetSuite export path and update billing-export runbook
